findings.title: New order() method is abstract and breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: Adding `int order();` as an abstract interface method is a source- and binary-incompatible change for any CryptoProvider implementation outside the three implementations updated in this PR (custom providers, downstream projects, test providers). Such implementations will fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError when loaded. It should be a default method (e.g. returning 0 or a documented neutral priority) so existing providers continue to work and can opt in to ordering.

findings.title: Equal order() values silently select an arbitrary provider instead of detecting ambiguity
findings.body: detectProvider now sorts by order() descending and silently takes element 0, but DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. If two of those are on the same classpath (the exact situation that previously threw 'Multiple crypto providers loaded'), the winner now depends on ServiceLoader iteration order rather than any intended priority, so an application can silently run with the non-FIPS provider in FIPS mode or vice versa. Ties at the highest order need to remain an error, or the providers need distinct, intentional order values.

findings.title: ES384/ES512 tests reuse a default-curve key pair and only assert a self round-trip
findings.body: The constructor generates one EC key pair with no ECGenParameterSpec, i.e. the JCA default curve (normally P-256), and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. The ES384/ES512 cases therefore never produce real 48- or 66-byte R/S components and only assert asn1->RS->asn1->RS returns the same bytes, which would still pass for DER output that a JDK Signature verifier would reject. Each algorithm should use its matching curve (P-256/P-384/P-521) and the converted DER signature should be verified with Signature.verify (and vice versa) to prove interoperability.
